preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or have gained ownership)
LP burn must be enabled (lpBurnEnabled = true)
Sufficient time must have passed since last LP burn (block.timestamp >= lastLpBurnTime + lpBurnFrequency)
Uniswap V2 pair must hold MarvinInu tokens

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, wait for lpBurnFrequency (default 3600 seconds) to pass since lastLpBurnTime, then execute a sell transaction to the Uniswap pair. This will trigger autoBurnLiquidityPairTokens() which burns a percentage (default 0.25%) of LP tokens, reducing total supply and increasing the attacker's relative token holdings. Alternatively, use manualBurnLiquidityPairTokens() directly if cooldown period has passed.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has an automatic liquidity pair token burning mechanism that burns tokens from the Uniswap pair when selling to automated market maker pairs. This reduces the total supply in the pair, creating a deflationary effect. An attacker can trigger this burn and then sell their tokens at a higher price due to the reduced supply.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate owner to enable trading and set optimal burn parameters. 2. Buy tokens to establish a position. 3. Trigger the automatic LP burn by selling a small amount after the burn cooldown period. 4. Sell remaining tokens at the higher price post-burn.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner and call enableTrading(). 2. Use deal() to get ETH for buying tokens. 3. Buy tokens via the Uniswap router. 4. Warp time forward to pass lpBurnFrequency. 5. Sell a small amount to trigger the automatic burn. 6. Sell remaining tokens to profit from the price increase.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The token has transaction limits and fees that could cause arithmetic issues. We need to buy and sell amounts that respect maxTransactionAmount and account for fees properly.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Buy a smaller amount that respects maxTransactionAmount. 2. Account for fees when calculating sell amounts. 3. Use smaller transactions to avoid limits.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Buy a smaller amount (e.g., 1 ETH worth) to stay under limits. 2. After triggering burn, sell in smaller chunks to avoid maxTransactionAmount. 3. Check balances before each swap to ensure we have enough tokens.
attempts.failure_reflection: The arithmetic underflow/overflow likely occurs during the swap due to fee calculations or exceeding transaction limits. The token has maxTransactionAmount and maxWallet limits that we need to respect. Also, we need to ensure we're not trying to swap more tokens than we have after fees.
